description:
## Finding

\`ChatBackend::apply_space_metadata_patch\` at backend.rs:557-563
documents the return:

> Returns \`Ok(Some(updated_space))\` if the backend modified any
> properties beyond what the client requested (RFC 8620 §5.3
> server-set field echo, e.g. a normalised \`name\`); or
> \`Ok(None)\` if the patch was applied verbatim with no
> server-side modification.

(Same shape as the \`update_object\` finding in .59 but on a
different method.)

## What's ambiguous

A production backend that bumps a \`Space.updatedAt\` /
\`Space.lastModifiedAt\` / membership-count denormalization on
every successful metadata patch — which is normal bookkeeping
for any real backend that supports \`/changes\` — **never hits
the \`Ok(None)\` branch**. So either:

- \`Ok(None)\` is reserved for \"no observable side effect that
  the client should learn about\" (in which case timestamp
  bumps live in the not-shown-to-client space, separately from
  the wire-visible payload), OR
- \`Ok(None)\` is a vestigial path that real backends never use
  (in which case why document it?)

The doc gives no guidance. A third-party implementer guesses
inconsistently across object types, and the \`Ok(None)\` path may
work for some types and not others, producing wire output that
is internally inconsistent across the kit's surface.

## Recommendation

Either:

1. Restate as outcome-keyed: \"Return \`Ok(None)\` if the wire-
   visible \`Space\` shape (after RFC 8620 §5.3 server-set field
   echo) is identical to the input patch applied to the prior
   state. Otherwise return \`Ok(Some(space))\`. Server-internal
   bookkeeping such as \`updatedAt\` timestamps that the client
   reads via \`Space/get\` MUST be reflected in the \`Some\` path
   if the field is part of the public \`Space\` shape.\"

2. Remove the \`None\` branch entirely (replace \`Option<Space>\`
   with \`Space\` in the return type) and let callers compute
   the echo-vs-modify distinction themselves if they need it.

Choice (1) is the lower-cost; (2) is a breaking change.

## Engineering basis

Direct read of backend.rs:557-563. The \`jmap-chat-types::Space\`
shape would need a separate verification pass for whether it
includes a public \`updatedAt\` field (the explore subagent did not
verify this), but the contract gap exists regardless: the doc
does not tell the implementer what to do.

## Related findings

.59 (foundation method docs thinness) covers the equivalent gap
on \`update_object\`. The two methods document the same semantic
shape (\`Option<O>\` for echo-vs-modify) but in different prose;
neither resolves the timestamp-bump ambiguity.
title: API contract: apply_space_metadata_patch Ok(None) vs Ok(Some) semantics ambiguous when backend bumps timestamps on every successful write
